To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we developed a new technique for singularity detection in cardiac tissue that is efficient and robust, that we developed a method for singularity detection closer in time to the initiation event, that we developed an analytic model for filament interactions in three dimensions that is in agreement with experimentally observed behavior, that we developed methods to include optical depth effects in three-dimensional filament models, and that we demonstrated the utility of a whole-heart geometric reconstruction as a visualization tool for singularity tracking.

the detection and tracking of phase singularities in cardiac tissue is a viable tool for investigating cardiac fibrillation dynamics, that filament interaction dynamics are governed by a critical bifurcations, that the inclusion of optical depth into a numerical filament model is necessary for accurate epicardial reconstruction of the dynamics, and that the geometric reconstruction of a heart with the fluorescent signal as a texture map provides a viable method for whole-heart singlularity visualization.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing new methods for visualizing and analyzing the complex dynamics underlying cardiac arrhythmia and defibrillation.
the detection and visualization of phase singularities and filaments in cardiac electrodynamic activity, and their interaction with each other and the tissue.
the visualization and analysis of the complex electrodynamic behavior of cardiac tissue.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a combination of experimental and computational techniques is necessary to understand and predict cardiac fibrillation.
a better understanding of cardiac arrhythmias is possible through the application of nonlinear dynamics and topology to optical mapping of the heart.

the phase-singularity-based techniques developed in this thesis have proven to be a useful and efficient method to detect and track phase singularities and filaments in cardiac optical mapping experiments.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the techniques developed here have the ability to localize, track, and visualize the electrodynamic behavior of cardiac fibrillation in a three-dimensional whole heart preparation, and that this information may prove to be a valuable tool in the understanding of fibrillation initiation, termination, and maintenance.

the use of phase singularities to characterize cardiac dynamics is both efficient and effective, and that a geometric reconstruction with the fluorescence information as a texture map is a viable tool for singularity detection.
we have developed and tested a method for singularity detection in optical mapping experiments, which has been shown to be robust, efficient, and capable of singularity detection near initiation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the phase singularity detection method is a powerful technique for analyzing the dynamics of cardiac arrhythmias, and can be used in a variety of contexts.
the use of topological charge as a means to detect phase singularitites and filaments is both efficient and robust, and can provide a new perspective on cardiac dynamics.
the topological charge of a phase singularity is a powerful tool in the detection and analysis of fibrillation behavior.
